title: Scoring live traffic: sampling what to grade, and the cost of grading it

videos.script: Rules see the form of a reply. Whether it answers the question needs something that reads. {{judge}} So a second model grades the first. On live traffic there is no answer key, so it can judge relevance and faithfulness, and not correctness. {{criteria}} Graded on everything, the week says seventy-seven percent before the release and sixty-two after. That took twelve hundred judge calls. {{all}} A tenth of the traffic, chosen at random, says roughly the same, but its intervals overlap. It cannot prove the release did harm. {{uniform}} The replies customers disliked say ten percent. True of those replies, and nothing like the week. {{targeted}} How sure a sample is depends on how many replies it holds, not on the size of the traffic. {{sizes}} And every judgement has a price. Here, a quarter of what the reply cost to write, per criterion. {{cost}} A sample is how a team grades every day and still pays for it. {{end}}
